Corpus census: 135 DriverDataTableLookupAndTimeConversion call sites in f1c_ida_decompiled/functions (114 literal, 21 variable in 18 functions); the literal and dynamic emitters for eids 151-160 and the sub-clip resolver chain were read in full. Owner exe read-only (F1 Challenge Online.exe in 99-02 (V10)): event table 0x5BF9A0 + eid*0x14. No live game.
owner_exe_check: Event rows 151-169 read from owner exe: priority 70 for 151-156 and 55 for 157-169; cooldown 20.0 only for 154, else 1.0 (matches dump); score = dump score.
subclip_findings: The sub-clip resolver (MapCollisionShapeToBoneIndex, sub_412C30) maps number N to SDT indices 153-189 (odd when a4=0, even when a4=1). Two live number routes exist: (a) eid 272 'X laps to go' (AIRetirementVehicleFailureEvent:75, player, race) -> even slots 160-168 for X=11,12,15,20,25; (b) eid 21 'AI pits, completed X laps' (AISessionPhaseChange:17, qualifying, AI, X<12) -> odd slot 169 for X=11. So SDT 160-169 are also lap-number slots. The SDT names at these indices (penalties and wins) conflict with that use: isolation test needed before any play plan relies on them.
contradictions: doc56 / dump label of eid 155 (PWS_PENALTY02, SDT 164) is 'Speeding in pits penalty'; code emits 155 for 'Jumped start' (AI counterpart 254) and owner triage says jump start. Speeding in pits is eid 153 (SDT 162).
doc56 label of eid 154 (SDT 163) is 'Blocking blue penalty'; code emits 154 for 'Ignored Blue Flags'.

Lap-number slots: SDT 160-169 are the number-word sub-clips used by 'X laps to go' (eid 272) and 'AI pits completed X laps' (eid 21), while doc56 and the dump name these indices as penalty and win clips. Either the names are wrong or the number route plays a different clip. Not resolved.
